newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour backs report on rail franchise breaches.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour backs report on rail franchise breaches.

text.p: The opposition Labour Party on Friday backed a report by a voluntary watchdog group, which claimed that at least two passenger rail operating firms were in breach of their service requirements.

Transport spokesman Andrew Smith said it showed that the government, having privatised the railways, was failing to stand up for passengers' interests. "It is only right that they (the firms) deliver the services or pay a penalty," he said.
But the Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (OPRAF) has dismissed the report, which focused on the 1996 summer timetable of Stagecoach Holdings Plc's South West Trains and Connex South Central.

It said in a statement issued on Thursday that there were "insignificant mismatches" with the Passenger Service Requirements and that in any case, the timetables had been developed by British Rail before privatisation.

The report, by the Railway Development Society, said for instance, that on the London to Portsmouth Harbour route, operating by South West Trains, the requirement was that 90 percent of fast services should have a maximum 89 minute journey time.
In fact, it said, seven of 16 weekday services were due on the timetable to make the journey this quickly.
Smith said in a statement: "Passengers have a right to expect services meet committed standards."
He added: "OPRAF is failing in its duty to secure minimum service requirements."
Labour has pledged to abolish OPRAF and replace it with a new body with a broader remit to oversee the railway industry.
